title: Texas governor's race, 9 days of posts

clusters.event: YouGov Texas poll: Talarico 50-44, Hinojosa 48-47
clusters.text: A UMass Lowell/YouGov poll of Texas likely voters finds Greg Abbott ahead of Gina Hinojosa, 48% to 44%.
clusters.verdict_basis:
UMass Lowell's Center for Public Opinion lists a UMass Lowell/YouGov poll of 850 likely Texas voters. 
It was conducted Sept. 18 to 28, with an adjusted margin of error of 4.5%.
 Political Wire reported that 
the poll finds Abbott (R) leading Hinojosa (D) 48% to 44%, with Pat Dixon (L) at 1%.
 Newsweek gave the same figures and added that 
Abbott's lead is within the margin of error.
 Later Newsweek and Yahoo/Austin-area poll roundups still list the UMass Lowell result as Abbott 48%, Hinojosa 44%.

The claim's numbers, pollster, and population (likely voters) all match. The poll was published around Oct. 8, two days after the claim was first seen on X (Oct. 6). The claim doesn't state a release date, so I did not treat that as an error. I could not open UMass Lowell's own release, only its poll index page. The figures come from Newsweek and Political Wire. Other polls cited in the same coverage show a closer race, and some show Hinojosa ahead. That doesn't change the accuracy of this claim.

lanes.label: Abbott is solid and will win

clusters.event: YouGov Texas poll: Talarico 50-44, Hinojosa 48-47
clusters.text: A YouGov poll finds Hispanic voters in Texas back Gina Hinojosa over Greg Abbott, 58% to 37%.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Newsweek reported on a YouGov survey of 3,622 likely voters, conducted Sept. 28 to Oct. 5, 2026. 
It had Hinojosa narrowly ahead of Abbott, 48% to 47%.
 The same report says 
Hinojosa leads Hispanic voters 58 percent to 37 percent
, which matches the claim's numbers and candidates. RealClearPolling lists the same poll with the same sample size, dates and topline (
Abbott 47, Hinojosa 48
), so the poll exists. I found the 58–37 crosstab only in Newsweek and did not find YouGov's own release. Other YouGov-branded polls give different Hispanic splits, such as 
51 to 43 in the UMass Lowell/YouGov poll
 and 
56–42 in the UT/YouGov poll
. The claim's figures match the Sept. 28–Oct. 5 poll specifically, so it holds as worded. Hispanic subgroups are small samples with wider margins of error than the 3-point topline.

clusters.text: In recorded audio, Ken Paxton said Greg Abbott is struggling in his reelection bid.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Rolling Stone published audio from a Sept. 24 private fundraiser in Washington, D.C. 
In the audio, Paxton says "Yes, Abbott is struggling."
 
He adds that the race is "still close" even though Abbott has name ID and money advantages over Hinojosa.
 Mediaite, Newsweek, Raw Story and the San Antonio Current report the same quote. 
In a second exchange Paxton says Abbott is "struggling, but he has a lot of money."
 The claim matches the reporting. Two caveats: the recording was made privately by an attendee and leaked, and I did not hear the audio myself, so I'm relying on outlets quoting it. 
Paxton's spokesperson called it "cherry-picked audio" and a partisan hit job.
 The spokesperson's statement, as quoted, does not dispute that Paxton said it.

clusters.text: Greg Abbott lowered Texas flags to half-staff for the third anniversary of the October 7 attack in Israel.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The governor's office issued a press release dated October 6, 2026. It says Abbott ordered the U.S. and Texas flags at all state buildings lowered to half-staff on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, in solidarity with Israel and in honor of those killed in the Hamas attacks.
 
Abbott's statement opens with "Three years ago...", which matches the third-anniversary framing.
 The Houston Chronicle, the Austin American-Statesman and the Dallas Express also reported the order. 
The Dallas Express described it as marking three years since the attack.
 
The flags were to return to full-staff at sunset the same day.
 So the order covered one day, and the claim's wording does not say otherwise.

clusters.text: JB Pritzker and the Democratic Governors' Association are each sending $1 million to Gina Hinojosa's campaign.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The New York Times reported this on Oct 7, 2026. GV Wire carried the text of that report. It said Pritzker and the DGA 
are each sending $1 million to support her bid, Pritzker and a top DGA official said Tuesday
. A DGA executive director's statement in the same piece called the money 
the group's latest investment in Gina Hinojosa's campaign
. The Hill also reported that 
the DGA and Pritzker announced this week that they each plan to give $1 million
. The Week said both are putting 
"at least $1 million"
 toward her election. One secondary aggregator (eciks.org) said Pritzker's gift was $1.2 million. That conflicts with the NYT account, and it is a weaker source. The core claim matches the primary reporting, which rests on on-record statements from Pritzker and the DGA. I did not find a campaign finance filing confirming the contributions.

clusters.text: A UT/Texas Politics Project poll finds Gina Hinojosa narrowly ahead of Greg Abbott, 49% to 48%.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The UT/Texas Politics Project's own release on its latest poll reports 
Hinojosa holding a statistically insignificant one-point lead over the incumbent, 49% to 48%, with 3% preferring "someone else"
. KXAN reports the same figures and says 
the poll of 1,200 registered Texas voters was conducted Sept. 25 through Oct. 5, with a margin of error of +/- 2.83 points
. The 49–48 figure applies to likely voters (
49% support among likely voters, compared with 48% for Abbott
). The Texas Tribune and Houston Chronicle also report it, and the Tribune calls it 
effectively a tie
. "Narrowly ahead" is therefore accurate, though the lead is well inside the margin of error. The earlier UT/TPP poll in August had Abbott ahead 45–40, so this is a new result. A separate Marist poll showed Abbott ahead, which doesn't affect what this claim says about the UT/TPP poll.

clusters.event: UMass Lowell/YouGov poll: Senate tied 45-45, Abbott 48-44
clusters.text: Gina Hinojosa invites Greg Abbott to debate her at the Governor's Mansion next Thursday at 10 AM.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Hinojosa's own X post, dated Oct. 8, 2026, says 
"Governor Abbott, I'll meet you at the Governor's Mansion next Thursday at 10 AM," and that if he's not man enough to debate her, he doesn't deserve to be governor.
 Her campaign press release says she held a San Antonio press conference 
calling on Abbott to debate her in front of the Governor's Mansion in Austin on October 15th at 10am.
 Oct. 8 was a Thursday, so "next Thursday" is Oct. 15, which matches. The San Antonio Current and CBS Austin later reported that her team sent Abbott proposed debate terms and that she planned to appear at the mansion regardless. One nuance is that the venue is the mansion's front steps or outside the mansion, not inside it. That doesn't change the substance of the claim. The claim only says she invited him, and it doesn't say he accepted. Reporting says 
Abbott hadn't said whether he'd participate.

clusters.event: Oct 7 anniversary: Abbott orders flags to half-staff
clusters.text: Greg Abbott did not lower flags or mention the third anniversary of the Uvalde school shooting.
clusters.verdict_basis:
I found no primary record or news report that covers Abbott's actions on the third anniversary, May 24, 2025. The reporting I found covers other years.
   - Abbott's office issued a flag order and a moment-of-silence call for the one-year anniversary in 2023 (
gov.texas.gov press release
).
   - For the second anniversary in 2024, 
Fox News reported the shooting was not mentioned on his social media accounts or in his office's press releases
. That report also covered State Sen. Roland Gutierrez's criticism of the omission.
   - For 2025, the only coverage I found was 
a Texas Public Radio report on local events marking three years since the shooting
. It says nothing about Abbott or flags. A partisan Substack post skips 2025 entirely.
   - Abbott's 2024 silence suggests the claim is plausible, but it doesn't establish what he did in 2025. The governor's 2025 press releases and flag orders weren't in my results, so I couldn't confirm either the flag half or the "mention" half. "Mention" is also broad, since a social post or remark would count.

In recorded audio, Ken Paxton conceded Republicans will likely lose seats in the Texas legislature.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Rolling Stone reported on Oct. 14, 2026, that audio of a private donor event shows Paxton conceding Republicans will likely lose seats in the state legislature.
 The quoted line is that 
Republicans are "going to probably lose some seats" in the Texas legislature
. HuffPost gives a slightly different wording: 
he doesn't see the Legislature "getting better" for Republicans and says "We're probably going to lose some seats."
 Mediaite and Newsweek report the same remark. 
Mediaite says he conceded this "to Democrats."
 The audio is 
from a Sept. 24 fundraiser, recorded by an attendee who opposes Paxton's candidacy.
 Paxton's side didn't deny the remark. His spokesperson 
called the leak "cherry-picked audio from a private fundraiser"
 and a "partisan hit job." Paxton also said 
clipped remarks don't necessarily reflect what he meant.
 I didn't find the full audio, and I haven't independently listened to it. The claim rests on Rolling Stone's clip, which other outlets corroborate. The remark is a prediction by Paxton, not evidence that seats will actually be lost. The claim as worded doesn't say otherwise.

clusters.text: A Texas homeowner told a canvasser for Greg Abbott he would absolutely not support Abbott.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The exchange in the claim did happen, but in June 2022 during Abbott's race against Beto O'Rourke, not the 2026 race against Hinojosa. 
The man, later identified as Dr. James Whitfield, answered "Absolutely not."
 
He first posted the doorbell-camera video on Twitter, and it showed canvasser Monique Dawson at his door.
 The canvasser's link to Abbott was also disputed. 
Dawson said she worked for Grassroots Advocates, a company contracted to canvass for Abbott.
 
Abbott's office said she had never been employed by Texans for Greg Abbott or volunteered for the campaign.
 My searches found no 2026 incident like this one. Posted on 2026-10-11 with no date, the claim reads as current news, and that reading is wrong. The wording is also loose on whether she was an Abbott canvasser.
